newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit slips but recovers on Negara presence.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit slips but recovers on Negara presence.

text.p: * Ringgit slipped but recovered quickly as Bank Negara checked rates after Bank of Thailand said it would allow a managed float of the baht
* Profit-taking and commercial selling pulled dollar/ringgit down from 2.5250
* Weak dollar/yen also limited dollar/ringgit upside
The ringgit slipped against the dollar after the Bank of Thailand said it would allow a managed float of the baht, but recovered quickly on Bank Negara's presence, dealers said.
Some dealers said Bank Negara was just checking on rates but others said the central bank did intervene.
"They came in at 2.5248/50 this morning" through its agent bank, said a senior dealer at a large Malaysian bank.
Dealers said profit-taking and commercial selling then pulled dollar/ringgit back down to around 2.5210/20. The ringgit's recovery was helped by a weaker dollar/yen, they said.
Dealers and analysts said the baht's floatation and corresponding sell-down has not affected the ringgit adversely.
"In fact it has done the opposite," said research house MMS International in its market commentary.

"Bidders, mostly offshore parties, are pre-occupied with the baht and having bought dollar/baht aggressively, are suspected to have covered some of their long dollar/ringgit positions in return," it said.

Thailand's Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Wednesday that effective immediately the country's exchange rate system would be a managed float, whereby the value of the baht would be set by market forces.
Dealers said they expected dollar/ringgit to continue trading in the 2.5200-2.5250 range.
Over the past week, dollar gains have been capped by fears of central bank intervention. There has been talk of Bank Negara placing orders to sell the dollar at 2.5250.
Bank Negara intervened last Friday to sell an estimated $100 million to support the ringgit at 2.5250 a dollar after a heavy attack on the local currency.
At 0230 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5220/30 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5246/50 in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
